original_question: What structural consequences for central simple algebras can be deduced from bounds on essential dimension or essential p-dimension? In particular, can one bound ed(CPAlg_n) and ed(Alg_G), compute ed(Alg_G) - ed(G), and determine whether equality ed(CPAlg_n) = ed(PGL_n) forces every degree-n algebra over every field extension of F to be a crossed product?
target_in_paper: §6, Problem 6.4 in the Essential dimension section, together with the immediately preceding Essential dimension and crossed products paragraph that defines CPAlg_n and Alg_G. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact three numbered tasks of Problem 6.4: bounding ed(CPAlg_n) and ed(Alg_G), computing ed(Alg_G) - ed(G), and asking whether the equality ed(CPAlg_n) = ed(PGL_n) forces all degree-n algebras over all field extensions of F to be crossed products. It also correctly places the question in the paper’s essential-dimension/crossed-product interface. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
missing_details: The paper fixes a base field F and works with functors on Fields_F, i.e. field extensions K/F with F-embeddings; your draft does not specify this ambient category. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
G is not arbitrary: in the setup before Problem 6.4, G is a finite group of order n >= 2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

CPAlg_n and Alg_G need explicit definitions: CPAlg_n(K) is the set of isomorphism classes of crossed product central simple K-algebras of degree n, while Alg_G(K) is the set of isomorphism classes of G-crossed product central simple K-algebras of degree n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

For full stand-alone precision, crossed product and G-crossed product should be understood in the paper’s §0 sense, i.e. via a maximal torus/maximal subfield that is Galois over the base field, respectively with specified Galois group G. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
The symbol ed(G) in ed(Alg_G) - ed(G) means the essential dimension of the finite algebraic group G over F, as in Definition 6.1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

The official problem is framed as drawing conclusions from essential (p-)dimension bounds, but the three concrete subquestions in Problem 6.4 are stated using ordinary essential dimension ed; your draft slightly blurs this by suggesting parallel explicit ed_p versions of the CPAlg_n and Alg_G questions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
The phrase every degree-n algebra should be made explicit as every central simple K-algebra of degree n for every field extension K/F. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

Useful hidden context immediately preceding the problem is that ed(CPAlg_n) = max_{|G|=n} ed(Alg_G) and ed(Alg_G) <= ed(CPAlg_n) <= ed(PGL_n); this is why the equality case in part (3) is structurally meaningful. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

Problem 6.4 itself is stated without any characteristic restriction; characteristic hypotheses such as char F not dividing n enter only in nearby partial results like Proposition 6.6. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
refined_question: Fix a base field F, an integer n >= 2, and a finite group G of order n. Let Fields_F be the category of field extensions K/F with F-embeddings, let CPAlg_n(K) be the set of isomorphism classes of crossed product central simple K-algebras of degree n, and let Alg_G(K) be the set of isomorphism classes of G-crossed product central simple K-algebras of degree n. With ed taken over F, and with ed(G) denoting the essential dimension of the finite algebraic group G, determine what structural conclusions about degree-n central simple algebras can be extracted from essential-dimension bounds by: (i) finding bounds for ed(CPAlg_n) and ed(Alg_G), (ii) computing ed(Alg_G) - ed(G), and (iii) deciding whether the equality ed(CPAlg_n) = ed(PGL_n) implies that every central simple K-algebra of degree n, for every field extension K/F, is a crossed product. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at §6, Problem 6.4 rather than the neighboring computational Problem 6.2: the symbols CPAlg_n and Alg_G are introduced only in the Essential dimension and crossed products paragraph immediately before Problem 6.4, and the three concrete requests in the draft match items (1)-(3) there almost verbatim. Definition 6.1 supplies the meanings of ed and ed_p, while the paragraph just before Problem 6.2 identifies H^1(-,PGL_n) with the functor of degree-n central simple algebras. Proposition 6.6 is the nearby supporting result the authors themselves single out, because they explicitly note that it resolves Problem 6.4(2) for G = C_n when char F does not divide n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
